articles.title: The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays - Engadget
articles.text:
The first batch of Android XR smartglasses made me rethink my stance on specs without displays
I still want models with built-in screens, but Google’s first run of intelligent eyewear has a lot to offer.
The first device powered by Android XR came out last year when Samsung released the Galaxy XR headset. But this fall, Google is taking its augmented reality platform in a different direction with the launch of intelligent eyewear from partners such as Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. This gives Google its own version of lightweight smartglasses to rival competitors like the third-gen Ray-Ban Meta line, and after testing them out, it made me reconsider my feelings about smart specs without built-in displays.
As this first generation of intelligent eyewear is a bit of a departure from previous Android XR devices, I think it's important to get some of the basics out of the way first. For this family of specs, Google is in charge of the OS while Samsung is handling much of the tech — including things like the cameras, mics, touch sensors and more. All of that then gets handed over to Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, who are in charge of the glasses design, lenses, general sales and customer support.
Right off the bat, this seems like a great division of responsibilities because it allows each company to do what they're best at. Google handles the software, Samsung takes care of the hardware and the real glasses makers ensure you have good-looking frames with the right prescriptions (you can even opt for transition/photochromic lenses). And right out of the gate, it feels like there's already a lot of interesting styles and color combos to choose from, regardless if you're a bit more fashion-forward or if you, like me, prefer a more traditional frame.
Another important thing to note is that while Gentle Monster's eyewear will be a touch more expensive than Warby Parker's models ($449 and $395, respectively), they will have the same general tech specs. Those include the same 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage, a 12MP camera (that also handles up to 3K video), stereo speakers, far-field mics and a built-in touch sensor. Battery life is also the same across the board with around nine hours of use on a single charge, while the case for the glasses stores enough juice for multiple full charges.
Furthermore, you won't be required to have a paid Gemini plan to use any of the features of the glasses; it's all free. These glasses will even work with both Android devices and iPhones with feature parity across both OSes. That said, there won't be any options with a built-in display, which means Google won't have a true rival to the Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, at least not yet.
When it comes to features, it's no surprise that these glasses have a lot of overlap with the Ray-Ban Meta specs. There's a physical button near the right temple for capturing images: A short press takes a picture while a long press records videos. There's also a touch sensor built into the right arm for doing stuff like controlling volume, pausing audio or dismissing Gemini. And of course, the glasses are connected to your phone wirelessly (either Bluetooth or Wi-Fi depending on the situation) so you have access to streaming music, notifications, messages, supported apps and more. However, the real lynchpin of the entire platform is Google's AI, which can be easily summoned via voice controls or by performing a long press on the touch panel.
Now I'll admit that I don't interact with Gemini all that often when I'm using a phone or a laptop. When I already have access to a screen, a keyboard and all sorts of dedicated apps, so I find I can often perform tasks faster manually than asking an AI assistant to do them. But when wearing smartglasses, it's a whole different story. If you want to respond to a text, get turn-by-turn directions or start some tunes, you can do all that hands-free with simple voice commands while keeping your phone in your pocket. Granted, that is sort of table stakes for smartglasses these days, but being able to walk around with your head up while dodging traffic or other pedestrians can't be understated.
But it goes deeper, because thanks to Gemini's intelligence and persistent memory between conversations, the AI in your glasses has a much deeper understanding of how to help you. Instead of constantly having to say a wake word all the time, you can have more natural back and forth dialogue. This allows you to get updates on your events, make adjustments to questions and pick up on previous queries even when they happen throughout the course of your day (you can specify how long you want Gemini to remember conversations).
Where things get really interesting is the combination of computer vision and AI, which allowed me to do things like pick up a physical invite card and simply ask Gemini to add it to my calendar. No need to grab my phone, open up an app and add details like the time, date and location myself. I was also able to do things like simply look at a bunch of different ingredients and ask Gemini to make a smoothie from what was in front of me. It can even do rough estimates for how much of a certain food has been added, so if you're not worried about being super precise, you can leave your measuring cups in a drawer. And if you run out of certain foods, you can easily tell Gemini to add something to your grocery list.
Then there are other features like live translation, which feels kind of magical. The glasses are designed so that the mics are directed in a cone-shaped space in front of you, so that even in a room with other conversations going on, the glasses don't get confused. Not only does this let you switch speakers naturally just by looking at someone else, Gemini will even adjust the output of a translation to sound similar to the original speaker. This allows you to follow along in real-time almost as well as someone who speaks the language naturally.
That said, the thing that impressed me the most about these Android XR glasses is the platform itself. Compared to some rivals where a lot of features feel like a work in progress, Google's OS feels much more mature. This includes little touches like dedicated sounds when Gemini accesses your camera, when the glasses take a photo or video, when Gemini leverages external AI and more. Google has done a pretty good job of translating a lot of the most important features you use on your phone to a medium without a screen.
Then there's Google's approach to privacy, which looks to be a step up from the competition. In addition to each pair of glasses coming with an LED indicator that blocks you from taking pictures or videos when it's covered up or disabled, Google also isn't supporting features like livestreaming video directly from the specs. Furthermore, Google says images and info sent to Gemini will stay on your device and will not be used to train AI or for ad targeting. That might not sound like much, but considering Google owns YouTube and generates billions from advertising, the simple act of leaving money on the table in favor of privacy is a welcome departure from Meta's glasses. Those have always felt like they are meant to expand the reach of Facebook and Instagram.
The one caveat to all this is that you do have to buy into talking to and relying rather heavily on Gemini. I'm still not sure I'm 100 percent on board with that, but at least for me, these glasses make a better argument for always-on AI support than almost any other class of device I've used. So while I'm still waiting for companies to deliver streamlined specs with built-in displays, these audio-first options feel like much more than a stepping stone towards that. They're surprisingly full-featured, and I don't think it's a stretch to say that compared to rival assistants like Siri, Muse and others, Gemini is the smartest of the bunch. So even if you primarily want these for playing music, keeping tabs on your schedule and getting occasional help from AI, Google's first batch of Android XR-powered intelligent eyewear feels like it's already jumped to the front of the pack.
Pre-orders for the new family of Android XR intelligent eyewear from both Warby Parker and Gentle Monster begin today with official sales slated for December 10.

articles.title: Humble Bundle redesign removes two-factor verification from settings
articles.text:
The Humble Bundle storefront for buying games and other software recently got a new look, but on the settings page, it no longer offers a way to add or update two-factor verification methods, as reported by Kotaku. PC Gamer also points out that there are Humble Bundle support pages discussing two-factor verification, and the writer for the publication said that they had set up two-factor verification on the old version of the site.
Humble Bundle redesign removes two-factor verification from settings
A new look for the Humble Bundle storefront is missing an important security feature that was previously there.
However, it does appear that, at least as of now, there is some form of two-factor verification. When I tried logging into my Humble Bundle account while writing this article, I was prompted to check my email for an access code before I could access my account. While logged in, I was able to update my password, but I didn’t have to enter my old password to be able to do so.
For what it’s worth, my passwords app also shows that I set up a rotating two-factor code for Humble Bundle at some point. I was not asked to input that at any part of my login process today.
Humble Bundle owner IGN Entertainment and IGN parent company Ziff Davis didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News.
Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.
The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees. Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

articles.title: Lợi nhuận lao dốc, Bkav Pro tiếp tục khất nợ 161 tỷ đồng gốc trái phiếu
articles.text:
Tiếp tục khất nợ trái phiếu
CTCP Phần mềm diệt virus Bkav (Bkav Pro), doanh nghiệp do ông Nguyễn Tử Quảng làm Tổng Giám đốc kiêm người đại diện pháp luật, vừa công bố thông tin về tình hình chậm thanh toán gốc và lãi trái phiếu.
Theo đó, doanh nghiệp không thanh toán được gần 7 tỷ đồng tiền lãi lô trái phiếu mã BKPCB2124001 theo kế hoạch ngày 26/5/2025. Đối với nghĩa vụ trả nợ gốc gần 161 tỷ đồng, Bkav Pro mới thanh toán được 1,076 tỷ đồng vào ngày 6/11.
Lý do được đưa ra là tổ chức phát hành chưa thu xếp đủ nguồn tài chính để thực hiện nghĩa vụ thanh toán. Doanh nghiệp cho biết đang đàm phán với người sở hữu trái phiếu.
Lô trái phiếu BKPCB2124001 được phát hành năm 2021, ban đầu có lãi suất 10,5%/năm, sau đó được gia hạn đến tháng 5/2025 với lãi suất 11%/năm. Nguồn vốn huy động được sử dụng để phát triển camera AI View, chuyển đổi số và một phần hoạt động sản xuất Bphone. Tài sản bảo đảm gồm cổ phần Bkav Pro và một số tài sản liên quan đến ông Nguyễn Tử Quảng.
Việc phần lớn nghĩa vụ gốc và lãi vẫn chưa được thanh toán cho thấy doanh nghiệp chưa giải quyết được bài toán dòng tiền, dù khoản nợ đã được gia hạn.
Lợi nhuận giảm mạnh, công nợ quá hạn lớn
Áp lực tài chính của Bkav Pro còn thể hiện qua kết quả kinh doanh. Báo cáo tài chính bán niên 2026 cho thấy Bkav Pro đạt hơn 1,32 tỷ đồng lợi nhuận trước thuế và khoảng 1,18 tỷ đồng lợi nhuận sau thuế, lần lượt giảm gần 57% và 54% so với cùng kỳ năm trước.
Đến ngày 30/6, vốn chủ sở hữu của doanh nghiệp đạt khoảng 267 tỷ đồng, trong khi tổng nợ phải trả lên tới 353 tỷ đồng.
Đà suy giảm lợi nhuận của doanh nghiệp đã kéo dài trong nhiều năm. Năm 2021, doanh nghiệp từng ghi nhận gần 100 tỷ đồng lợi nhuận sau thuế. Tuy nhiên, con số này giảm xuống 40,4 tỷ đồng năm 2022 và chỉ còn gần 4,44 tỷ đồng trong năm 2025.
Các chỉ số sinh lời cũng suy giảm. Tỷ suất lợi nhuận sau thuế trên vốn chủ sở hữu (ROE) giảm từ 1% xuống 0,4%; tỷ suất lợi nhuận sau thuế trên tổng tài sản (ROA) giảm từ 0,4% xuống 0,2%.
Với lợi nhuận bán niên 2026 chỉ đạt 1,32 tỷ đồng, khả năng tạo nguồn tiền để xử lý khoản nợ trái phiếu gần 161 tỷ đồng đang là thách thức lớn.
Đáng chú ý, báo cáo kiểm toán năm 2025 của Công ty TNHH Hãng Kiểm toán AASC lưu ý nhiều vấn đề liên quan đến các khoản công nợ và nghĩa vụ tài chính của Bkav Pro.
Trong đó, Bkav Pro có khoản phải thu cho vay ngắn hạn quá hạn đối với CTCP BKAV với dư nợ gốc 315 tỷ đồng và lãi 100 tỷ đồng nhưng chưa trích lập dự phòng. Ngoài ra, doanh nghiệp còn khoản phải thu khách hàng hơn 18,15 tỷ đồng quá hạn và khoản vay gần 33 tỷ đồng từ CTCP Dịch vụ và Đầu tư Trustlink đã quá hạn thanh toán.
Về triển vọng kinh doanh, camera AI View được xem là một trong những hướng đi đáng chú ý của Bkav Pro. Nhu cầu giám sát giao thông, an ninh đô thị, nhà máy, trường học và các hệ thống cảnh báo tự động đang mở ra dư địa cho thị trường camera thông minh.
Song lợi thế công nghệ chưa đồng nghĩa với lợi thế thương mại. Bkav Pro phải cạnh tranh với những thương hiệu lớn như Hikvision, Dahua cùng nhiều nhà sản xuất khác có lợi thế về quy mô sản xuất, giá bán và mạng lưới phân phối. Để đánh giá khả năng thương mại của AI View, cần xem xét số lượng dự án đã triển khai, doanh thu, khách hàng và khả năng duy trì hợp đồng.
Trong khi đó, Bphone là sản phẩm gắn với hệ sinh thái Bkav, nhưng phải cạnh tranh với các thương hiệu smartphone toàn cầu như Samsung, Apple, Xiaomi, OPPO và vivo, vốn có lợi thế lớn về chuỗi cung ứng, hệ sinh thái và marketing.
Với Bkav Pro, thách thức trước mắt không chỉ nằm ở việc phát triển sản phẩm mới mà còn là cải thiện khả năng tạo lợi nhuận, thu hồi các khoản công nợ quá hạn và giải quyết nghĩa vụ trái phiếu kéo dài. Quy mô lợi nhuận hiện tại còn rất nhỏ so với khoản nợ trái phiếu chưa thanh toán, khiến áp lực dòng tiền tiếp tục là vấn đề cần theo dõi.

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook is still down
articles.text:
Since just before 1PM ET on Thursday, reports have come in from around the world that people can’t access their Outlook email, either through the web or apps. Microsoft quickly acknowledged the issue from its Microsoft 365 Status account, saying that “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.”
Microsoft Outlook is still down
Microsoft 365 issues have been cutting people off from their email since early Thursday afternoon, and they still aren’t fixed.
There were also some reports of problems with Teams, but not to the same extent, while Microsoft’s official updates said customers may experience issues across its suite of 365 business services. Microsoft comms director Ben Hope said in a statement that “We are aware and investigating reports of users experiencing issues with Microsoft 365 services, primarily issues with Exchange Online. We appreciate our customers’ patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.”
Several hours later, Microsoft has gone through several variations of update notes regarding the issues and its attempts to fix them, saying it’s had problems rebooting servers and being able to monitor their health. As of about 6PM ET, Microsoft has a note saying it’s managed to get some of the affected servers running:
We’ve begun returning a portion of the affected servers to service, and they’re remaining stable so far. We’ve also shifted traffic and connections to alternative pathways wherever possible and have observed limited recovery in some regions.
We’ve streamlined our recovery process to expedite returning the remaining affected servers to service. To further support recovery, we’re implementing protective traffic management measures in a specific location to reduce load on the affected infrastructure, and we’ll expand these measures to additional locations if we observe positive results. As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect to the service.
There’s still no ETA for full restoration, but we will continue to monitor this ongoing outage.
Update, 6:23PM ET: Added latest status update from Microsoft.

articles.title: Anthropic lets companies run Claude's agent service on their own servers
articles.text:
Anthropic now lets companies run Claude Managed Agents in their own cloud or data centre. Agent histories and credentials stay on their systems, but each model call still goes to an outside provider such as Anthropic or AWS.
Anthropic now lets companies run its Claude Managed Agents service on their own servers, Help Net Security reported. The self-hosted version launched on Thursday, and customers must request access through their Anthropic account team, the company said in its release notes.
Managed Agents is Anthropic’s service for running AI agents that use tools and remember past sessions. Customers could already run the agents’ tools on their own machines, but Anthropic ran the rest, including the stored history and credentials.
Now customers can run the whole service in their own cloud account or data centre. Agents, session histories and credentials stay on their systems, and every tool call can be logged.
There is a catch. Each time the agent asks Claude a question, the conversation still goes to a model provider, such as Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry. Customers choose which one, but Claude itself does not run inside their network.
Customers also take on the work Anthropic used to do, such as securing and updating the server. Nothing moves over from Anthropic’s hosted service, so agents and saved data must be rebuilt, and some features, such as webhooks and scheduled runs, are missing.
The move gives cautious companies more control over where agent data lives. That matters in Europe, where ECB president Christine Lagarde has warned of the risk of relying on foreign AI. Rivals such as Mistral have long pitched sovereign AI as the answer.
OpenAI took a different route in September, letting companies run its agents inside Amazon’s cloud. Nvidia, meanwhile, has built hardware for safer agents.

articles.title: “Đây là phần RAM tôi chưa dùng”: Công cụ tự động gửi báo cáo hằng ngày cho Sam Altman để cà khịa cơn khát RAM của OpenAI
articles.text:
Sau phát biểu gây tranh cãi của CEO Open AI Sam Altman về việc sở hữu RAM trên máy tính cá nhân là "lãng phí", cộng đồng công nghệ đã lập tức có những màn "cà khịa" đỉnh cao. Tiêu biểu nhất là Ram-Altman - một công cụ mã nguồn mở do IainKay phát triển.
Theo thông tin từ cộng đồng phát triển phần mềm và các trang tin công nghệ quốc tế, Ram-Altman là một script dạng Bash có cơ chế hoạt động cực kỳ lầy lội, cứ định kỳ 5 phút, công cụ này sẽ âm thầm kiểm tra dung lượng RAM khả dụng trên máy tính của người dùng.
Nếu phát hiện phần bộ nhớ trống vượt mức 10%, script sẽ tự động tổng hợp số liệu và bắn một email báo cáo trực tiếp đến hòm thư được cấu hình sẵn – mà cụ thể ở đây là nhắm đến vị CEO của OpenAI. Nhiều dân mạng hài hước bình luận rằng nếu Sam Altman thực sự là người nhận những email này, có lẽ tốt nhất ông nên... đừng bao giờ mở hộp thư ra xem nếu không muốn bị "tra tấn" bởi lượng RAM rảnh rỗi của hàng triệu game thủ và lập trình viên. Bạn đọc quan tâm có thể tìm hiểu thêm về dự án này trực tiếp trên GitHub với từ khóa IainKay/ram-altman.
Điểm hài hước nằm ở chỗ tác giả đã soạn sẵn hàng loạt mẫu email với tiêu đề và nội dung xoay xở đủ các góc độ châm biếm: "Báo cáo Sam: Máy tôi đang lãng phí thêm 8GB RAM hôm nay." hay "Gửi thuyền trưởng OpenAI: Thanh RAM nhà tôi chỉ mới chạy 5% công suất, xin nhận lỗi vì đã làm cản trở tiến trình tiến hóa của AI toàn cầu!".
Tác giả IainKay cũng cài đặt giới hạn để công cụ chỉ gửi tối đa 1 email/ngày nhằm tránh biến nó thành một cuộc tấn công từ chối dịch vụ (DDoS). Tuy nhiên, dân mạng nhận định rằng nếu có hàng chục nghìn người cùng cài đặt script này, hòm thư của Sam Altman chắc chắn sẽ chìm ngập trong biển thông báo về những thanh RAM "đang ngồi chơi xào nước" trên khắp thế giới.
Trò đùa này bắt nguồn từ một phát ngôn trước đó của Sam Altman. Cụ thể, vị giám đốc điều hành OpenAI cho rằng từ góc độ phân bổ toàn cầu, việc để nguồn cung DRAM khan hiếm của thế giới nằm yên trong các máy tính cá nhân – nơi chúng chỉ được sử dụng một phần nhỏ thời gian là một sự lãng phí "khá tồi tệ". Theo ông, để phục vụ cho các trung tâm dữ liệu AI khổng lồ trong bối cảnh thiếu hụt nghiêm trọng, điện toán đám mây mới là nơi cần tối ưu hóa tối đa.
Ngay lập tức, phát biểu này vấp phải làn sóng phản ứng dữ dội từ cộng đồng PC toàn cầu, đặc biệt là những người ủng hộ quyền tự chủ phần cứng và phong trào chạy AI cục bộ (Local AI). Cư dân mạng và các nhân vật nổi tiếng trong làng công nghệ (thậm chí bao gồm cả tỷ phú Elon Musk) đã lên tiếng châm chọc quan điểm này. Cộng đồng cho rằng người dùng bỏ tiền ra mua phần cứng thì có toàn quyền định đoạt cách họ sử dụng, và việc lưu trữ RAM trên thiết bị cá nhân là sự lựa chọn thuộc về quyền riêng tư cũng như chủ quyền số của mỗi người, thay vì phải "dâng" hết tài nguyên cho các đám mây AI.
Cho đến nay, phía OpenAI và Sam Altman vẫn chưa đưa ra bình luận chính thức nào về công cụ Ram-Altman. Nhưng với việc script này đang lan truyền với tốc độ chóng mặt trong cộng đồng sysadmin và lập trình viên Linux, rất có thể hộp thư của Sam Altman sẽ còn tiếp tục nhận được hàng nghìn "lời báo cáo tự giác" mỗi ngày về từng megabyte RAM đang nằm nghỉ ngơi thong thả trên máy tính của người dùng./

articles.title: Five ways Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia could damage the AI industry | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s confession that he had an affair (and reports of another one with a direct report) that led the board to oust him on Thursday isn’t just your run-of-the-mill salacious billionaire CEO sex scandal.
In this case, one of his lovers is suspected by the U.S. government of being a spy for China. She’s also an executive of a Singapore-based neocloud that is suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China.
These affairs show undeniably poor judgment by Huang and, I’d argue, unchecked hubris on many levels. Such choices are not only a betrayal of his wife of 40 years, they’re also a liability for his company. Sleeping with any Nvidia partner is bad enough, but he also chose one in a tinderbox of a geopolitical situation. Even if Alice Huang’s company wasn’t suspected of helping Chinese firms evade chip restrictions (and he was somehow unaware of this), it was still exploiting a legal loophole by renting powerful AI infrastructure to Chinese companies.
It’s those potential national consequences that may land him in a hellscape of ongoing public humiliation. Republican committee chairs are already summoning him to testify in closed-door sessions about the security ramifications.
Will Democrats, who are set to take over key committees when the new Congress convenes in January, also haul him in to testify on the Hill? No one knows yet, but Huang has flaunted his close relationship with President Trump. Remember when Trump called him while he was onstage at the All-In Summit in September? Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom, a deeply unpopular project with American voters. Several Democratic lawmakers have already vowed to investigate the money behind it.
In other words, he is a billionaire close to Trump. He was — until Thursday — the face of AI and data centers (also a deeply unpopular political topic with voters), and he has publicly admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Even though he’s no longer CEO, that seems too juicy a target for Democrats to ignore.
Beyond whatever may be coming, Huang’s influence has been lost right when he was using it to push the tech industry in a number of directions. These areas have now lost their biggest champion.
Open-weight AI models as competitors to closed-source labs
Huang has been the biggest, loudest advocate for open-weight AI models in the tech industry and among government policymakers. Nvidia not only offers its own open-weight models, it also offers a lot of other open source tech for agents, AI security, and more. It has even agreed to acquire the biggest site that hosts them, Hugging Face, for $12.9 billion. (That deal is supposed to close in the first half of next year, pending regulatory approval.)
In July, when Anthropic and OpenAI were reportedly urging the Trump administration to ban Chinese open-weight models, Huang organized a letter of support for open-weight models generally (if not Chinese models specifically), signed by hundreds of tech companies.
Open-weight models give enterprises choice in the market and reduce costs. Without Huang, the next biggest advocate for them is perhaps Microsoft’s Satya Nadella, but he’s not out there organizing the industry to speak up.
Pushing the AI industry to clean up its security
Both OpenAI and Anthropic revealed incident after incident this year as their AI agents hacked into others’ networks or performed other misdeeds. Huang loudly proclaimed the AI industry still didn’t need regulation and would deal with safety itself.
As the industry mulled over what they should do (auditors? a FINRA-like board?), Huang rallied the tech industry again. Nvidia got over 100 companies to sign on to his Open Agent Safety Platform, a largely open source effort to solve the epidemic of misbehaving AI agents.
Naturally, this effort hasn’t instantly solved the problem, and now the top spokesperson for self-regulation via technology solutions is out of his position of influence.
Arguing AI is a tool, not a life form
Huang has also been among the loudest voices insisting that AI is an engineered system that creates products, and so can be controlled like any other engineered system. This viewpoint counters the AI doomers and even the big AI labs themselves, which sometimes position their models as on the verge of consciousness (Anthropic) or as alien minds (OpenAI).
While Huang deals with the fallout of his actions, the loudest voice of this counter-narrative is, for the foreseeable future, silenced.
A new Nvidia-powered AI PC industry
Huang also just convinced a long list of PC makers to buy into his long-time dream of providing CPUs (the main processor chips) for them. In this age, when most Americans have not experienced AI beyond a chatbot, he orchestrated a new line of high-end AI PCs geared for running agents locally.
These new PCs are due out this holiday season, and they may sell well for their intended targets: creators, developers, and others already savvy with agents. But now that Huang has become a meme for cheating on his wife with an alleged spy, he’s perhaps not the best choice to help market these devices as a cool alternative to the Mac mini.
Financial engineering to fund data centers
Huang demolished his reputation right as bond underwriters (lenders) and bond buyers are pretty much over AI build-out-related debt. Of roughly $80 billion in data center bonds issued this year, nearly half were rated high-risk “junk,” Forbes reports.
Undeterred, Huang has been coming up with ways to continue financing the boom and keep his company’s revenues growing. Certainly, he’s authorized a mind-boggling number of so-called circular deals, where Nvidia buys stakes in companies to fund their expansion so they can buy chips. By some accounts, the company had committed to $750 billion in such deals as of July, Bloomberg reported. In August, Nvidia got even bolder, agreeing to backstop $105 billion in financing for an OpenAI data center in Ohio, CNBC reported.
Huang also convinced a whole new set of financiers to pony up. In August, he announced that deep-pocketed PE firms Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR had committed up to $500 billion for data center build outs. He promised them that the data centers’ Nvidia GPUs could be used as collateral because Nvidia was guaranteeing the chips would retain value.
Huang sold a vision of Nvidia as “investable infrastructure” with a long resale cycle, like airplanes. Then he made the rounds with the financial press, as he often did, to pitch his vision. Now, however, Wall Street is concerned that Nvidia’s stock will crash and take their portfolios, and possibly the economy, with it.
Nvidia has lost its top salesperson and the AI industry has lost its top hype man. Even if Huang somehow comes back into the public eye to champion AI again, every interview and meeting will be about his sex life, choices, and national security — not his vision for the industry.
We’ll have to wait and see how Nvidia navigates the scandal Huang heaped onto it, but now that the company is finally in its post “founder mode” era, and hunting for a new CEO, it’s doubtful it has the cache to push the industry the way Huang was.

articles.title: Nintendo is ending Google and Apple sign-ins early next year - Engadget
articles.text:
Nintendo is ending Google and Apple sign-ins early next year
The company is asking users to set up a password or a passkey for their Nintendo accounts.
Nintendo will discontinue Google and Apple log-ins early next year, so you may want to update the way you sign into your account soon. Starting on January 26, 2027, it will no longer be possible to sign into your Nintendo account, or to create a new one, with Google and Apple as a log-in method. In addition, it is also ending the My Nintendo Platinum Points mission that rewards you for linking your Google with your Nintendo account.
The company had made the announcement in a support page, where it also said that the exact end time of Google and Apple sign-ins depend "on the progress of the system change work." Nintendo is asking users to set up a password or a passkey before January 26. To set up a passkey, go to the Accounts page, sign into your account, choose Sign-In and Security Settings, select Passkeys and then Edit. From there, you can choose Register New Passkey to start signing into Nintendo with your device's authentication method.
Nintendo didn't say why it's removing Google and Apple sign-ins, and whether it has security concerns with them. Whatever Nintendo's reason for it, you may want to get your log-in sorted if you want uninterrupted access to your games and to the eShop.

articles.title: J.Crew launches an AI stylist built on Anthropic's Claude
articles.text:
J.Crew has launched Style Advisor, an AI stylist on its US website built with Anthropic’s Claude. Shoppers describe an occasion and get complete outfits from looks J.Crew’s stylists put together. Personal recommendations based on past purchases will come later.
J.Crew has launched Style Advisor, an AI stylist on its website built with Anthropic’s Claude, Anthropic announced on Thursday. It is available in the US for women’s and men’s clothing.
Instead of searching for a sweater, then trousers, then shoes, shoppers can describe what they need, such as an outfit for a beach wedding or a first job interview. Style Advisor replies with complete looks, and shoppers can keep refining them. They can also start from one item and ask what goes with it.
Every suggestion comes from outfits J.Crew’s own stylists put together for the brand’s catalogue shoots. The AI picks and shows those looks rather than inventing new ones, which keeps it in line with the brand’s style.
“We see an opportunity to fundamentally rethink the shopping experience,” said Libby Wadle, CEO of J.Crew Group.
J.Crew built the tool using several Claude models. In each conversation, the mid-sized Sonnet 5.5 acts as the stylist, while the smaller Haiku 5.5 handles quick tasks so answers come fast. For now, it does not tailor suggestions to each shopper’s past purchases, but J.Crew plans to add that and expand to more countries.
Retailers are racing to add AI stylists. Ralph Lauren launched its Ask Ralph assistant late last year, and Kate Spade uses Amazon’s shopping AI, while Zalando’s agent will shop other retailers from 2027. On Prime Day, shoppers sent by AI assistants were more likely to buy than those from search.

articles.title: Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu
articles.text:
Microsoft is starting to test new customization options for Xbox consoles today. Xbox Insiders will be able to start testing new rotating backgrounds, new library options for digital games, and the ability to move the Xbox Guide menu to the right-hand side.
Xbox owners are getting more customizations for backgrounds and the Guide menu
Xbox Insiders get to test the new features today.
Xbox Insiders get to test the new features today.
“Xbox Insiders can now save favorite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle through them automatically,” says Eden Marie, principal software engineering lead at Xbox. “You can also choose Shuffle at the start of any background category. Have your background change each time you sign in, or set it to change hourly, daily, or weekly.”
Microsoft is also improving how you organize disc-to-digital games on an Xbox console. Xbox Insiders who have claimed a digital license from a disc-based game will be able to see these titles in a separate category in the library section. You’ll also be able to hide the digital license icon on game tiles.
Finally, Xbox Insiders will be able to choose whether the Guide menu appears on the left or right side of a screen. “Alpha Skip-Ahead members can try them first,” says Marie. “We’ll bring them to more Xbox Insiders and players over time.”

articles.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company, but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday, suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. He wrote that Cook has “an unparalleled track record of succeeding a bigger-than-life founder,” in reference to Cook taking over from Apple founder Steve Jobs.
Whether or not Trump agrees with this opinion, or is simply blasting off an idea that hopped into his mind, is anyone’s guess.
“Tim Nvidia,” however, doesn’t quite have the same ring as “Tim Apple” does.

articles.title: Cú sốc hạ tầng AI: Gần một nửa dự án trung tâm dữ liệu ở Mỹ hiện đang mắc kẹt hoặc "chết yểu" vì vấp phải "kẻ thù" không ngờ tới
articles.text:
Giữa lúc cơn sốt AI đang càn quét toàn cầu, một cuộc khủng hoảng trầm lặng nhưng tàn khốc đang diễn ra ở hậu trường, gần một nửa số dự án trung tâm dữ liệu dự kiến triển khai trong giai đoạn 2025–2026 đang rơi vào cảnh đình trệ hoặc bị hủy bỏ hoàn toàn.
Cơn sốt tính toán và cái bẫy "bỏ quên hàng xóm"
Khi cuộc đua xây dựng hạ tầng AI bùng nổ, các "ông lớn" công nghệ như Microsoft, Google, Amazon hay Meta từng đinh ninh rằng bài toán khó khăn nhất chỉ xoay quanh hai yếu tố là nguồn điện khổng lồ và quỹ đất xây dựng. Không một ai trong số các nhà đầu tư vạch ra chiến lược lại tính đến một biến số mang tính quyết định nằm ngay sát vách là những người hàng xóm.
Thực tế phũ phàng này đã giáng một đòn mạnh vào giới công nghệ. Hàng loạt dự án bị trì hoãn hoặc xóa sổ không phải vì thiếu chip hay cạn kiệt vốn, mà xuất phát từ làn sóng phản đối dữ dội từ phía cộng đồng dân cư địa phương.
Những người sống cạnh các đại dự án trung tâm dữ liệu đã không còn giữ thái độ im lặng. Họ đứng lên đấu tranh chống lại tiếng ồn hạ tầng từ quạt tản nhiệt, nguy cơ quá tải và tăng giá lưới điện sinh hoạt, cùng sự cạn kiệt nguồn nước làm mát. Trớ trêu thay, họ đang là những người chiến thắng trên bàn đàm phán chính trị lẫn pháp lý.
Khi những "gã khổng lồ" vấp phải bức tường phản kháng tại Mỹ
Cuộc đua xây dựng trung tâm dữ liệu từng được kỳ vọng sẽ tăng tốc không phanh để đáp ứng khát vọng tính toán của các mô hình AI thế hệ mới. Tuy nhiên, từ "thánh địa" trung tâm dữ liệu Virginia cho đến Georgia, Pennsylvania hay Delaware, việc hàng loạt dự án bị ngáng đường đang biến những kế hoạch tỷ đô thành tờ giấy vụn trên bàn làm việc.
Tại Virginia, nơi được mệnh danh là "thủ phủ" trung tâm dữ liệu toàn cầu với hàng trăm đại dự án của các tên tuổi lớn như Amazon (AWS) và Microsoft, làn sóng phản đối đang bùng nổ mạnh mẽ hơn bao giờ hết. Chỉ riêng trong giai đoạn vừa qua, hàng chục dự án đã phải đối mặt với kịch bản bị hủy bỏ. Người dân sinh sống tại các hạt Loudoun và Prince William liên tục xuống đường biểu tình và gửi đơn kiện tập thể, nguyên nhân trực tiếp đến từ việc các tổ hợp máy chủ khổng lồ này mọc lên quá sát khu dân cư và trường học. Sức ép từ cộng đồng lớn đến mức buộc chính quyền địa phương phải siết chặt quy hoạch và thắt chặt trong khâu cấp phép.
Dịch chuyển sang Georgia và Arkansas, làn sóng phản đối đã chuyển hóa thành các biện pháp đóng cửa pháp lý cứng rắn. Tại Georgia, nơi các cụm trung tâm dữ liệu ngốn hàng ngàn megawatt điện mọc lên như nấm sau mưa, phản ứng gay gắt từ cử tri đã đẩy giới chức chính quyền vào thế chân tường, buộc họ phải tính đến các lệnh tạm dừng cấp phép mới. Tình hình còn căng thẳng hơn tại Independence County (Arkansas), khi chính quyền địa phương không ngần ngại thông qua quyết định cấm hoàn toàn việc xây dựng các trung tâm dữ liệu mới kéo dài đến tận năm 2031.
Trong khi đó, tại Delaware và Pennsylvania, hàng loạt dự án tỷ đô đã bị các nhà chức trách thẳng tay khai tử dưới áp lực của người dân. Tại New Castle (Delaware), dự án hạ tầng dữ liệu có quy mô khổng lồ lên tới 1.200 MW đã buộc phải chấm dứt hợp đồng sau khi vấp phải sự phản đối dữ dội từ cư dân xung quanh. Kịch bản tương tự cũng diễn ra tại Upper Macungie (Pennsylvania), nơi đại dự án của EdgeConneX bị hội đồng địa phương từ chối thẳng thừng trong các phiên họp công khai, khép lại hy vọng bành trướng hạ tầng của nhà đầu tư.
Từ những buổi họp dân cư đầy căng thẳng cho đến các điều luật đóng cửa hạ tầng được thông qua, sự phẫn nộ của cộng đồng đang kéo dài thời gian hoàn thành các trung tâm dữ liệu thêm ít nhất 6 tháng so với dự kiến, đánh trực diện vào tiến độ thương mại hóa AI của các gã khổng lồ công nghệ.
Bài học đắt giá cho kỷ nguyên bùng nổ hạ tầng
Việc gần một nửa số dự án trung tâm dữ liệu lâm vào cảnh "chết yểu" hoặc chậm tiến độ là tiếng chuông cảnh tỉnh cho toàn bộ ngành công nghệ. Cuộc đua AI không chỉ đo lường bằng tốc độ gom chip hay tiềm lực tài chính, mà còn phụ thuộc vào năng lực đối thoại xã hội. Nếu không giải quyết được tiếng nói từ những người hàng xóm ở tuyến đầu, giấc mơ mở rộng kỷ nguyên AI sẽ mãi chỉ nằm trên bản vẽ chiến lược.

articles.title: Whoop just launched a social network | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Whoop, the maker of screen-less fitness bands, is launching a social network on Thursday that lets its members follow friends and family and share their health data.
The network, called Whoop Humans, will be rolled out in the Whoop app to members at every membership tier at no extra cost. Members can follow anyone on Whoop and choose what to share, from sleep and recovery to workouts and achievements. Followers can react and comment; members can also attach photos and commentary to their data. It’s all opt-in, CEO Will Ahmed tells us.
Whoop already has a social feature, Teams, which a little more than half its customers use, according to the company. But Teams is built around groups and leaderboards, and everyone in a group sees everyone else’s information. Humans is meant to be more intimate. Members decide who follows them and who sees what, so a trainer can track a set of clients without the clients seeing one another’s data, for example.
I found myself questioning how much a spouse wants to know about the other’s sleep score when Ahmed mentioned this particular scenario, so I asked him how else beta members used these newer social features. He said the company learned that people were more engaged when someone reported a low recovery score than a nearly perfect one, suggesting that the new feature may be particularly helpful for understanding when someone is struggling and might need attention.
Indeed, the bigger story here is where Whoop continues to be headed, which is into medical wellness. Like its most direct rival, Oura, the company is pushing faster and more aggressively into the wellness opportunity that an aging population presents.
Whoop had already added FDA-cleared ECG and atrial fibrillation detection, blood pressure insights, blood testing, and medical-record uploads. Asked if older customers are gravitating to Whoop, Ahmed said, without offering specifics, that Whoop has seen “huge growth” among people over 60 over the past 18 months. He also said his was among the first companies accepted into a Medicare program that reimburses qualifying wearables that can show they improve health outcomes, and that it now has Medicare members.
He added that he expects families to be big users of Humans. (You can imagine adult children checking in on aging parents.)
But the company’s efforts to be thought of as the “brand for personal health” raises questions, naturally, about privacy. Ahmed said members choose which metrics to share, can remove followers, and can switch on “stealth mode” to go dark for a few days without changing their settings. Activities marked sensitive aren’t shared by default, and Ahmed said health alerts and medical information aren’t shared at all. Members can also report any comment or photo that they deem disturbing, and the company said reported content is reviewed.
As for minors, Whoop’s minimum age is 13 for all members (higher in some countries), meaning customers of that age can share their data subject to consents and privacy settings. Asked whether a parent could follow a teenager’s data, he didn’t answer directly and pointed to the privacy controls.
Ahmed also said Whoop doesn’t sell member data. “Our product is not you; it’s the membership,” he said, adding that the company doesn’t license data to third parties.
He was candid about dealmaking. Asked about Oura’s announcement this week that it will pay $625 million for Counsel Health, a service offering on-demand physicians, Ahmed said he expects “more consolidation” among AI-focused, clinician-focused, and wearable companies, and that Whoop is always on the prowl. Its deep relationship with members, he said, puts it “in a position to be an acquirer.”
He was more guarded about the company’s own finances, declining to share revenue or say whether Whoop is profitable. He did say that the company now has about 1,200 employees, membership on its software platform has increased more than 70% a year for three years running, and that it expects to have nearly 4 million members by year-end.
As for an IPO (the company raised a very big round earlier this year), he said only that Whoop “will certainly IPO in the future.” He also wouldn’t comment on Oura, which shelved its own IPO of up to $2.2 billion in September citing market uncertainty.
In the meantime, Whoop is widening its reach. The company announced that its devices will be sold through Ulta stores beginning next March (around 500 locations of the beauty retailer to start, and a target to retail in more than a thousand stores eventually). Indeed, Ahmed said Whoop’s female audience has more than doubled from last year.
As for competition, in addition to Google’s new Fitbit Air band, Whoop may soon have to contend with Apple, which is reportedly developing a Whoop-style band. But Ahmed mostly shrugged off those concerns, suggesting that building a product doesn’t guarantee success. Instead, he said, Whoop’s job is to stay true to the “aspiring” people it serves.

articles.title: Apple Support Community forums close on 20 November after 28 years
articles.text:
Apple has stopped taking new posts on the Apple Support Community and will close the forum on 20 November. The site has been read-only since 10 November, according to a notice on its homepage.
“You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site,” the notice says.
9to5Mac’s Marcus Mendes first reported the notice on the evening of 10 November. The last post appears to have gone up at 5:49pm Pacific time that day, Joe Rossignol reported for MacRumors.
Apple told MacRumors it made the decision after a careful evaluation of strategy and customer needs.
Nearly 30 years of answers
The forum launched in 1998 as Apple Tech Exchange, according to MacRumors. It became Apple Discussions in 2000, Apple Support Communities in 2011 and Apple Support Community in 2022.
The notice does not say what happens to the old posts. Apple told AppleInsider it will take the forums completely offline, William Gallagher reported on 11 November.
Apple has not read the forums in at least five years, according to AppleInsider’s sources. The sign-in button now leads to an internal portal for Apple’s corporate employees, MacRumors reported.
Where users can go
MacRumors pointed users to Apple Support, its own forums and Reddit. Reddit is moving to login-only viewing, and it now uses AI to summarise product threads.
Customers can still contact Apple Support directly, MacRumors noted. Last month, Apple Support took on Apple’s offer to replace iPhone Duos with failing inner screens.

articles.title: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
articles.text:
Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including “questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests.” The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses. It’s available starting today in search, the Gemini app, all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and in Google Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, says it’s “now the new default model in AI Mode & being used for your hardest questions in AI Overviews.”
Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’
Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen also gives users a wider range of links in its responses by “conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics.” Its responses have more visuals, too, like images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. One of Stein’s examples shows the AI generating an interactive animated driving simulation in response to a user’s question about how phones locate which lane of a highway a car is on in areas without cell service. Google says the new model also has improved language understanding “across all supported AI Mode languages.”
Users have more thinking level options with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, as well, including low, medium, high, and a new “xhigh” mode. According to Google, the new model “delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence” compared to Gemini Flash 3.8, and it “matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class,” like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.

articles.title: Người dùng Facebook chú ý thông báo mới nhất của công an
articles.text:
Công an vừa thông tin về thủ đoạn chiếm quyền Facebook tinh vi với mục đích lừa đảo, chiếm đoạt tiền.
Phòng An ninh mạng và phòng, chống tội phạm sử dụng công nghệ cao, Công an TP Đà Nẵng đã phát đi cảnh báo về thủ đoạn chiếm quyền tài khoản Facebook thông qua các đường link giả mạo tài liệu học tập.
Theo thông tin từ cơ quan công an, em A.T. mới đây truy cập một đường link được chia sẻ trên Facebook với nội dung “Tổng ôn kiến thức môn Địa lý lớp 12” để tìm tài liệu phục vụ học tập. Tuy nhiên, sau khi nhấn vào đường link, website yêu cầu đăng nhập tài khoản Facebook nhưng không cung cấp nội dung học tập như quảng cáo.
Sau đó, tài khoản Facebook của A.T. xuất hiện dấu hiệu bị người khác đăng nhập và sử dụng danh nghĩa cá nhân để nhắn tin với mục đích lừa đảo, chiếm đoạt tiền. Rất may, chưa có ai trở thành nạn nhân của thủ đoạn này.
Phát hiện bất thường, A.T. nhanh chóng đăng xuất tài khoản khỏi các thiết bị và đổi mật khẩu, cho rằng sự việc đã được xử lý. Tuy nhiên, đến ngày 8-11-2026, em tiếp tục nhận được tin nhắn đe dọa từ các đối tượng. Đáng chú ý, những người này còn sử dụng hình ảnh cá nhân của em để chỉnh sửa, gây áp lực, ảnh hưởng đến tâm lý và danh dự của nạn nhân.
Từ vụ việc trên, Công an TP Đà Nẵng nhận định, các đối tượng đang lợi dụng nhu cầu tìm kiếm tài liệu học tập, đề thi, đề cương ôn tập miễn phí để giăng bẫy người dùng. Thông qua các đường link được chia sẻ trên mạng xã hội, chúng dẫn dụ nạn nhân truy cập website giả mạo, sau đó yêu cầu cung cấp thông tin đăng nhập tài khoản Facebook.
Khi có được thông tin, các đối tượng có thể chiếm quyền kiểm soát tài khoản, mạo danh chủ tài khoản nhắn tin vay tiền, lừa đảo người thân, bạn bè. Không dừng lại ở đó, hình ảnh và thông tin cá nhân bị thu thập còn có thể bị khai thác để đe dọa, gây sức ép hoặc phục vụ những hành vi vi phạm pháp luật khác.
Để phòng tránh, Phòng An ninh mạng và phòng, chống tội phạm sử dụng công nghệ cao, Công an TP Đà Nẵng khuyến cáo học sinh, sinh viên không tùy tiện truy cập các đường link lạ, kể cả những đường link được giới thiệu là tài liệu học tập, đề thi hay đề cương ôn tập miễn phí. Người dùng tuyệt đối không cung cấp mật khẩu Facebook, mã OTP hoặc thông tin cá nhân trên các website không rõ nguồn gốc; chỉ đăng nhập thông qua ứng dụng hoặc địa chỉ chính thức của nền tảng.
Bên cạnh đó, người dùng cần kích hoạt xác thực hai yếu tố, thường xuyên kiểm tra lịch sử đăng nhập và đăng xuất khỏi những thiết bị không nhận diện. Khi phát hiện tài khoản có dấu hiệu bị chiếm quyền, cần nhanh chóng sử dụng các kênh chính thức để khôi phục tài khoản, đổi mật khẩu email liên kết và kiểm tra các thiết bị đang đăng nhập.
Đặc biệt, nếu bị đe dọa, sử dụng hình ảnh cá nhân để chỉnh sửa, phát tán hoặc tống tiền, nạn nhân không nên làm theo yêu cầu hay chuyển tiền cho đối tượng. Thay vào đó, cần lưu giữ toàn bộ tin nhắn, hình ảnh, đường link và thông tin tài khoản liên quan làm bằng chứng, đồng thời trình báo cơ quan công an để được hỗ trợ, xử lý.

articles.title: Axle raises $9M to bring AI agents to Wall Street's meeting-makers
articles.text:
Axle has raised $9M led by Eniac and Bonfire Ventures. It makes software that helps investment banks arrange meetings between investors and company management, and will add more AI agents. It says some of North America’s biggest banks use it.
Axle, a startup that makes software for investment banks, has raised $9M in a round led by Eniac and Bonfire Ventures, it announced on Thursday. Teamworthy Ventures also joined.
Axle works on what banks call corporate access. Banks arrange meetings between big investors and company bosses, analysts and industry experts. Those meetings help investors decide where to put money, and they shape which banks get their trading business.
CEO Sam Shapiro says much of this work still runs on old software, spreadsheets and manual scheduling. He worked in corporate access at Goldman Sachs before starting Axle, according to the company’s 2024 pre-seed announcement.
Axle puts conferences, investor meetings, roadshows and expert calls into one system. Clients can request meetings and see schedules through portals that need no login.
The company says it works with some of North America’s largest investment banks but did not name them. One bank started using Axle earlier this year and, within months, dropped three other providers.
The new money will go into AI agents that help bank staff understand clients and spot opportunities. Axle is also building tools to show how much the meetings are worth to clients.
AI startups are moving fast into banking. Berlin’s Taktile raised $110M from Goldman Sachs to automate bank decisions, and Anthropic has launched ready-made finance agents for Claude, while OpenAI sells a ChatGPT for finance.

articles.title: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia — who is Colette Kress, his interim replacement? | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately.
This is a shocking twist for one of the most valuable companies in the world, which designs the chips that make the AI boom possible. Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan. But Huang has now been ousted after reports that he had affairs with both an alleged Chinese spy and one of his direct reports at Nvidia.
While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?
According to Nvidia’s website, Kress has worked at the company since September 2013. Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
The California-based 59-year-old has a very limited social media presence — on Linkedin, she has commented some well wishes on former colleagues’ posts about their retirement. But as CFO, she’s been a regular presence on Nvidia’s earnings calls, making her a familiar figure for analysts covering the company.
According to Forbes’ list of America’s Richest Self-Made Women, Kress’ net worth is estimated to be about $1.2 billion. Her Forbes profile adds that she initially joined Nvidia in part because her two sons endorsed the company for its role in the video game industry, which it was best known for at the time.
“Nvidias strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said in a statement. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”
Nvidia is slated to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, when we will likely hear more from Kress about her plans for the company’s immediate future.

articles.title: ‘It’s a mistake’: reactions from tech leaders on Jensen Huang’s resignation
articles.text:
Nvidia announced this morning that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with a direct report. The situation surrounding Huang has unfolded quickly, with The New York Times only reporting on Friday that Huang and the suspected spy were “close” before other dominoes started to fall, leading to a swift fall from grace for one of the biggest names in technology. (Hours after Huang’s resignation was announced, Reuters reported that he also had an “intimate relationship” with another Nvidia employee.)
‘It’s a mistake’: reactions from tech leaders on Jensen Huang’s resignation
Many prominent voices in technology and the president of the US have publicly supported the former Nvidia CEO despite his ouster.
Prominent voices in technology have come out in support of Huang, with some calling the resignation a “waste” and a sad day for “all humanity.” The narrative among those leaders on X, at least, is that Huang’s resignation was rushed — perhaps an overreaction to salacious news stories about his personal life. Some others have had a more neutral reaction, commenting more on Huang’s achievements at the company’s helm. You can see a collection of those responses below.
President Donald Trump
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!”, Trump said on Truth Social.
Elon Musk, SpaceX and Tesla CEO
Elon Musk said in a reply to an X user that it would “be an honor” to hire Huang. He also replied to a post that said “You’d think we’d have learned from Steve Jobs and Travis Kalanick that one does not just simply replace the founder…” by saying “True words.”
Tim Sweeney, Epic Games CEO
Sweeney said that today is “A sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity. Jensen founded and ran one of the few companies to reach a massive scale while driving massive continued innovation and ubiquity, while others fell into the trap of ever-increasing extraction.”
Ahead of Huang’s resignation, Sweeney posted about how Huang “saved” a GDC 2015 presentation by dropping off a graphics card and said that “The dude truly is the visionary driver of the future of tech from the gaming GPU era to CUDA to AI supercomputers.”
Palmer Luckey, Anduril founder
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said last night, before Huang’s resignation was announced.
Matt Mullenweg, Automattic co-founder and CEO
Mullenweg reposted an X post that followed his brief September ouster as CEO: “Founder advice: If you don’t have a coup attempt every few years, you’re not hiring strong enough leaders.” He said, “Just putting this back out there, for no reason whatsoever.”
David Heinemeier Hansson, 37signals CTO and creator of the Omarchy Linux distribution
“What a waste,” Hansson said this morning, replying to his own post from hours before: “NVIDIA would be wrong to fire Jensen. His marital indiscretions are between him, his wife, and a reprimand from the board. Have some proportionality.”
Clément Delangue, co-founder and CEO of Hugging Face (which Nvidia recently acquired for almost $13 billion)
“This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened,” Delangue said. “It’s a really sad day! But I want to make one thing clear: we’ll keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever. This is too important to slow down now. Let’s go!
Changpeng Zhao, former Binance CEO
“It’s a mistake for Nvidia to let Jensen resign,” Zhao said.
Peter Steinberger, OpenClaw creator and OpenAI employee
“If that Spy’s goal was to destabilize one of the most successful American companies, they achieved their goal,” Steinberger said. “Ousting Jensen feels rushed and not right.” (“I agree,” replied Sweeney.)
Aravind Srinivas, Perplexity co-founder and CEO
Srinivas thanked Huang for “33 years of bold leadership” in a post this morning. “You built a small startup into America’s most valuable company, with relentless improvement. Your grit and perseverance should always be remembered. Your personal generosity with time and advice to founders like me has secured a bright future for America and AI.”
Jason Calacanis, All-In Podcast host
Calacanis reposted Trump’s post, tagging Tim Cook and telling him to “Keep the seat warm” for Huang while “the investigation is sorted out” and saying that “America needs you Mr. Cook.” Last night, he also said that Nvidia shareholders should “decide Jensen’s fate after the investigation is complete — not the press or online mobs.”
Lex Fridman, Lex Fridman Podcast host
In a post talking about how he has seen Huang show “kindness, humility, care to everyone around him,” Fridman said that “I’m in shock frankly at all of this, including the mass hysteria around it. I love America, and I think NVIDIA letting Jensen go is terrible for America. I stand with Jensen.”

articles.title: Grok Build left 35,000 apps open, SpaceXSI sales plans included
articles.text:
Anyone who found the address of a Grok Build app could open more than 35,000 of them, security firm Claroc found in research published on 10 November. Two dozen belonged to staff at SpaceXSI, the company that makes Grok. They held a confidential onboarding plan, a sales territory map and advertising proposals.
SpaceXSI took its own 24 apps offline after the report, Claroc said. It left the apps of other Grok users open. Ars Technica’s Dan Goodin reported that SpaceXSI started removing them within hours of his email asking about the findings.
What was open
Grok Build turns a description typed into a chat into a working app. The user can then publish it at its own address on grok.me. Claroc tried more than 43,500 of those addresses. Of the 37,571 still online, 35,578, or 94.7%, opened without any sign-in.
Most were games, landing pages and calculators. About one in ten held internal business or personal data. Claroc estimates that 650 to 800 apps held private data.
Claroc confirmed some cases by hand. They included one intensive care patient’s lab results, a hospital group’s roster of more than 3,500 staff, and a fire department’s shift board. One contractor’s timesheet app carried 18 accounts with their passwords in plain text, in code that every visitor’s browser downloads.
Besides SpaceXSI and X, Claroc identified 30 organisations, six of them in the Fortune 500. It named none. Ars Technica listed more. They include a Tesla service-centre scorecard naming 22 technicians and a roster for a US Navy logistics contract.
SpaceXSI’s own open apps included a map of 594 strategic sales accounts and eight X advertising proposals. Claroc said one proposal, to a US federal agency, carried a confidential label.
How the apps were found
Grok gives every published app its own hostname of random words, such as name.grok.me. Nobody needs to guess one. When a visitor opens an app, its name reaches passive DNS services. These commercial databases log internet lookups, and anyone with an account can search them.
Shared chats from Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini keep the secret part of the link in the path, Claroc said. DNS never sees it. Last month, the same method exposed Meta’s Muse links.
In the paid account Claroc used, the publish screen proposed “Anyone with the link” as the access setting. It also offered “Invited users” and “Only you”.
“AI app builders turned publishing into a few clicks, and the default answer to who can see it is everyone,” Asaf Aprozper, Claroc’s co-founder and chief technology officer, said in the firm’s report.
Claroc also built two test apps of its own. In a team customer list, Grok’s code added anyone who signed in with Google to the team before checking membership. An outside account could then read, edit and delete records, the firm said.
What SpaceXSI says
A representative for Cursor, the coding company SpaceX bought in August, responded in an email to Ars Technica.
“Apps are private by default and nothing goes public unless the creator chooses to share it,” the representative said, according to Ars Technica.
SpaceXSI also told a reporter that publishing takes several steps, including a legal notice, and that employee accounts start on “Only you”, Claroc said. Claroc’s answer is that the people who published the 35,578 open apps went through every one of those steps.
The representative said ChatGPT, Lovable and Bolt also make shareable links. Aprozper agreed that apps on Lovable, Bolt and Replit have the same exposure.
“However, Grok is where we found by far the most sensitive company data,” Aprozper told Ars Technica.
Claroc sells security tools for AI-built apps. It asked SpaceXSI to make “Only you” the default, move shared apps onto hard-to-guess paths, and warn builders when an app has a database but no sign-in. It is now notifying the affected organisations itself.
It is not the first data problem for Grok Build. In July, the tool sent entire Git repositories to xAI’s servers. In October, Musk said the merged company would be renamed SpaceXSI.

articles.title: Norwest pushes deeper into AI with new $4B fund | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Norwest, a firm backed solely by Wells Fargo, has raised a $4 billion fund as it sets out to invest more in AI. This is the eighteenth fund for the 65-year-old multi-stage investment firm, and its largest to date.
The fund will be invested across various sectors and multiple countries, notably the United States, India, and Israel. But the big story here is AI, and Norwest’s plans to expand its investment in this area.
Norwest said Thursday it aims to capitalize on AI startups developing products and services across core industries such as consumer, healthcare, and technology. The investment firm, which has backed Plaid, Spotify, Uber, and Vuori, said it will continue to expand its investments in physical AI, voice AI, agentic cybersecurity, and aerospace.
If that sounds like a broad approach, it is intended to be, Jeff Crowe, a senior managing partner at Norwest, told TechCrunch.
“We’re taking a broad approach to AI because its impact is broad,” Crowe added, as AI is not limited by industry, geography, or application. “Just as digital transformation did, AI transformation has the potential to touch most layers of enterprise, consumer, and healthcare solutions: networking, enterprise IT and applications. Adapting to an agentic environment means applying AI broadly across products and services that solve problems.”
Crowe added that the firm is particularly excited about early-stage companies building AI-native application and infrastructure, physical AI, domain-specific models, and cybersecurity solutions.
Some of the firm’s recent investments reflect this strategy. For instance, the firm invested in Coval, which builds tools to test and evaluate AI agents, and Generalist AI, a startup that has developed AI foundation models for robots.
Since the launch of its seventeenth fund, a $3 billion raise that closed in 2024, the firm has made more than 87 investments.

articles.title: The Oura Ring 4 is almost as good as the newer model, but $150 cheaper
articles.text:
The previous-generation Oura Ring 4 is on sale for as low as $249 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, $100 off the retail price, and the first big discount on the device since July. The price varies a bit by size and color, with most silver and black models in stock at the lowest price between sizes 8 and 13. Best Buy also has an exclusive deep blue “midnight” color in stock for $279. If you’re not sure about your size, you can pick up an Oura Ring 4 sizing kit for $10 at Amazon or Target, which includes $10 in store credit towards an Oura Ring 4 purchase.
The Oura Ring 4 is almost as good as the newer model, but $150 cheaper
Oura’s last-gen smart ring sports the same sensors and software as the latest version.
Oura Ring 4
The last-gen Oura Ring 4 is a little thicker, but offers much of the same software, sensors, and a wider range of sizes.
My colleague Victoria Song tested six different smart rings to compare their health and fitness tracking features, and Oura beat them all handily. The Oura Ring 4 improved on its predecessor with more accurate sensors, a slimmer design that leaves the competition in the dust, not to mention frequent software and feature updates. Accessing all of the features requires an active subscription, which is either $5.99 per month or $69.99 per year. The newer Oura Ring 5 is lighter and thinner, but otherwise includes the same sensors and software features as the Oura Ring 4. That makes this previous-generation deal even more appealing,

articles.title: OpenAI revenue hits $10bn a quarter as its adjusted losses widen
articles.text:
OpenAI’s revenue reached $10bn in the third quarter, up almost 50% from the second, The Information reported. OpenAI shared the figures with investors on Tuesday. Demand for its newer models and enterprise products had picked up, Valida Pau and Jemima McEvoy wrote, citing a person familiar with the matter.
It is the first quarter in which OpenAI’s revenue has reached $10bn, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Revenue was almost three times its level a year earlier, they said. OpenAI declined to comment to Bloomberg.
Losses still growing
The Wall Street Journal’s Berber Jin saw documents on the results. They show OpenAI’s adjusted operating margin improved to -109% in the third quarter, from -150% in the second. Its adjusted operating loss still rose, to $10.9bn from $10.1bn.
In the second quarter, OpenAI’s revenue grew 18% to $6.7bn, the Journal reported at the time. That left it behind Anthropic on quarterly revenue for the first time.
What drove the jump
Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president, spoke on the investor call. So did Sarah Friar, its chief financial officer, and product leader Thibault Sottiaux, Bloomberg’s Rachel Metz and Rebecca Torrence reported.
OpenAI revenue has regained momentum thanks to new models, aggressive price cuts and a bigger push into AI agents, according to Bloomberg. The company told investors it ended September with roughly $50bn in annualised revenue. That matches the $50bn run rate reported in October.
How it compares with Anthropic
Anthropic reported $16.96bn in revenue for the same quarter. It first disclosed it in its IPO filing on 2 November. Its operating loss was $567m, and its adjusted operating margin was 15%.
Anthropic’s growth has slowed. Its revenue rose about 47% from the second quarter to the third. It had jumped 144% the quarter before, its filing shows.
The two companies count revenue differently. Anthropic includes sales made through its cloud partners, while OpenAI counts only its share of some partner sales, TechCrunch noted.
Anthropic’s IPO is reportedly oversubscribed, and it is due to price on 18 November. OpenAI is completing a funding round at a $1.25tn valuation, Bloomberg reported. It has delayed its own listing until next year.
